- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates; add 1–1.5% to forecast for next 2–3 periods.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) — adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average, not 30d trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often lags — forecast should be adjusted to match 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is flat, model tends to drift upward — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 3 periods.
